root_cause.text: The nSVM LBR copy helper `svm_copy_lbrs()` unconditionally cleared/marked the destination VMCB’s `VMCB_LBR` clean bit dirty, even when the destination was nested guest state `vmcb12`, whose clean bits are not architecturally defined.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that "`svm_copy_lbrs() always marks VMCB_LBR dirty in the destination VMCB`" and that "`nested_svm_vmexit() uses it to copy LBRs to vmcb12, and clearing clean bits in vmcb12 is not architecturally defined`"; correspondingly, the patch removes `vmcb_mark_dirty(to_vmcb, VMCB_LBR);` from `svm_copy_lbrs()` and adds dirty marking only in callers that write to `vmcb01`/`vmcb02`, not `vmcb12`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Mark vmcb02's LBR state dirty after updating it so nested SVM correctly saves and applies LBR changes.
intent_record.what: A call to vmcb_mark_dirty(vmcb02, VMCB_LBR) was added after the conditional logic that copies LBR state into vmcb02 and before svm_update_lbrv(&svm->vcpu) in nested_vmcb02_prepare_save().
intent_record.how: This ensures the LBR field in vmcb02 is marked dirty after its contents are updated, so the modified LBR state is recognized and propagated correctly at runtime instead of potentially being skipped as unchanged.

intent_record.intent_summary: Mark vmcb01 LBR state dirty after copying LBRs in the non-LBRV nested VMEXIT path so the updated state is preserved.
intent_record.what: The change adds braces around the existing if/else that selects the source VMCB for svm_copy_lbrs(), and adds a new call to vmcb_mark_dirty(vmcb01, VMCB_LBR) in the else branch after copying LBR state from vmcb02 into vmcb01.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when nested LBR virtualization is not enabled for the guest, the code now explicitly marks the vmcb01 LBR field as dirty after updating it from vmcb02, ensuring the modified LBR state in vmcb01 is recognized and propagated instead of potentially being left unnoticed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove dirty-bit marking from svm_copy_lbrs() so the helper only copies LBR state without also updating VMCB dirty tracking.
intent_record.what: The call to vmcb_mark_dirty(to_vmcb, VMCB_LBR) was removed from the end of svm_copy_lbrs(), while the register field copies into to_vmcb->save remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, svm_copy_lbrs() still copies the LBR-related save fields from one VMCB to another, but it no longer marks the target VMCB's LBR state as dirty as part of that helper, preventing this function from unconditionally flagging the LBR area for update.

relevance_review.reason: The group changes are about when and where nested SVM marks LBR state dirty after copying/modifying LBR data, which directly overlaps the root cause involving incorrect dirtying of the VMCB_LBR clean bit in svm_copy_lbrs(), especially across nested VMCB state transitions.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement is the vulnerable operation because it unconditionally marks the destination VMCB's LBR state dirty inside svm_copy_lbrs(). When the destination is nested guest state vmcb12, its clean bits are not architecturally defined, so updating them here causes the bug described in the root cause.

Author: Maxim Levitsky <mlevitsk@redhat.com>
Date:   Tue Mar 22 19:40:45 2022 +0200

    KVM: x86: nSVM: correctly virtualize LBR msrs when L2 is running
    
    When L2 is running without LBR virtualization, we should ensure
    that L1's LBR msrs continue to update as usual.
    
    Signed-off-by: Maxim Levitsky <mlevitsk@redhat.com>
    Message-Id: <20220322174050.241850-2-mlevitsk@redhat.com>

bic_trace_step.reason: The added helper `svm_copy_lbrs(struct vmcb *to_vmcb, struct vmcb *from_vmcb)` unconditionally does `vmcb_mark_dirty(to_vmcb, VMCB_LBR);` after copying the LBR fields. The root cause says this is wrong when the destination is nested guest state `vmcb12`, because `vmcb12` clean bits are not architecturally defined. This commit introduces exactly that unconditional behavior in the helper. The snippet also shows the helper is used generically from nested paths: `svm_copy_lbrs(svm->vmcb, svm->vmcb01.ptr);` and `svm_copy_lbrs(svm->vmcb01.ptr, svm->vmcb);`, demonstrating the helper is intended for moving LBR state between VMCBs without any guard on what kind of VMCB `to_vmcb` is. There is no check to avoid marking dirty when `to_vmcb` is `vmcb12`, nor any alternative handling for nested guest state. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present, and the fix is not present in this commit.
